Paragraph:
Translation: While contemplating the objects of the senses, a person develops attachment for them, and from such attachment lust develops, and from lust anger arises.

Purport (Excerpt): One who is not Krsna conscious is subjected to material desires while contemplating the objects of senses... One who is not... in Krsna consciousness, however powerful he may be in controlling the senses by artificial repression, is sure ultimately to fail, for the slightest thought of sense pleasure will agitate him to gratify his desires.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Understanding the subtle, early-stage cognitive triggers that lead to psychological breakdown and compulsive behaviors.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna maps the first stages of the psychological ladder of fall down: passive contemplation (dwelling on an object) leads to emotional attachment (sanga), which intensifies into compulsive desire/lust (kama), which, when thwarted, inevitably manifests as anger (krodha).
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is shown that mental downfall does not happen suddenly; it begins with seemingly harmless, repeated mental contemplation of triggers.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Cognitive Cascade of Addiction: The step-by-step progression from thought to attachment to obsession
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Dwell Time / Rumination: Contemplating sense objects until emotional attachment forms
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Frustration-Aggression Link: The automatic birth of anger when intense desires are blocked

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dhyayato visayan (Contemplating or dwelling on sense objects)
Kama-krodha-utpatthi (The origin of desire and its transition into rage)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The journey away from spiritual consciousness begins in the subtle realm of thought. Simply dwelling on material pleasures creates attachment, which escalates into obsessive desire. When those desires face inevitable material obstacles, they ignite anger, disrupting spiritual alignment.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This verse outlines the psychological trajectory of cravings and addiction. It demonstrates that behavior starts with micro-contemplations. The moment we passively entertain a temptation, we build psychological attachment. As attachment turns into intense craving, any barrier to that craving produces immediate frustration and anger. Awareness of this early entry point is vital for emotional health.
